Quick CRM snapshot: 
- Product: VS Code extension for pair-programming + inline completions, built as a thin client that streams tokens to the editor.
- POC goal: <50ms token latency for local dev workflows, negligible jitter for 1-3 developers concurrently. Need streaming SSE/WebSocket support with reconnection and resumed KV-cache.
- From call (02/12): 'We want seamless inline suggestions that feel native — no UI lag, no long 'thinking' states.' — Head of Eng.
- Model/version pinning: Must pin to a specific model hash for reproducible completions during beta; want ability to fallback to a quantized variant when Dedicated capacity constrained.
- Auth & rate limits: Extension ships with per-seat API keys; concerned about accidental leaked keys and downstream shared quotas. Require token scoping and server-side rate-limiting hooks + per-user telemetry.
- Security: SSO/SAML mandatory for enterprise customers; audit logs + retention policy for suggestion data (30/90/365 day options). KMS integration for any persisted cache.
- Cost sensitivity: High on per-token costs given heavy autocomplete usage. Interested in Redwood Optimize suggestions (batching, prefix caching) and cost impact analysis.
- Implementation notes: front-end uses websocket streaming; needs server fallback to chunked HTTP streaming if websockets blocked. Wants an SDK example for VS Code extension (typescript) and a patch for auth middleware.
- POC metrics defined: p50 token latency, cold-start time for new session, token-cost per 1k completions.
